question.prompt:
Mr. Garcia asked the members of his health class how many days last week they exercised for at least \(30\) minutes. The results are summarized in the following bar graph, where the heights of the bars represent the number of students.

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_8_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

What was the mean number of days of exercise last week, rounded to the nearest hundredth, reported by the students in Mr. Garcia’s class?

solutions.explanation:
Each bar gives a number of students, so the mean must count each student's reported days. The bar heights for \(1\) through \(7\) days are \(1,3,2,6,8,3,2\), giving

\[
1+3+2+6+8+3+2=25\text{ students}.
\]

Multiply each day count by its bar height to find the total reported days:

\[
\begin{aligned}
&1(1)+2(3)+3(2)+4(6)\\
&\qquad+5(8)+6(3)+7(2)=109.
\end{aligned}
\]

The mean is \(109/25=\boxed{4.36}\) days, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). Averaging the seven bar positions equally would ignore how many students gave each answer.
solutions.title: Weight each day value by its graph frequency
